claim_verdicts.claim_text: Spironolactone can explain the initial onset of elevated potassium.

citations.quote: Spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily was started by outpatient cardiology on 2026-02-19 and taken daily since; last home dose the morning of 2026-03-01, per patient and pharmacy fill history.
Assessment: new hyperkalemia with acute kidney injury; etiology not yet clear (differential includes reduced renal potassium clearance, ACE inhibitor effect and recent spironolactone use).
Assessment: hyperkalemia, likely secondary to spironolactone.

claim_verdicts.why: Spironolactone was taken daily from 2026-02-19 until the morning of 2026-03-01, which precedes the first elevated potassium, so the timeline allows it. The 03-02 note lists recent spironolactone use in the differential, and the 03-04 note calls it a likely cause, so the hedged claim that it can explain the onset is supported.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The record does not confirm the cause of the initial rise; reduced renal clearance and ACE inhibitor effect remain possible alternatives. Cause (2026-02-19) precedes effect (2026-03-02T09:30) (date inherited from note header): temporally possible, but timing alone does not prove causation.
